title: Standardized Protocols from the Caenorhabditis Intervention Testing Program 2013-2016: Conditions and Assays used for Quantifying the Development, Fertility and Lifespan of Hermaphroditic Caenorhabditis Strains
protocol: Turn on water bath and set to 55°C.
Add the following ingredients to a 2 L Erlenmeyer flask for each liter of media: Agar 23.0 g, NaCl 3.0 g, Bacto Peptone 2.5 g, DI Water 1 L, and include a large stir bar.
Pour or autoclave 4 liters at once in a tray; use dummy flasks filled with mock media if necessary.
Autoclave the media at 121°C at 15 psi for 45 minutes.
Move the autoclaved media immediately to the 55°C water bath.
After cooling to 55°C, add ingredients in the following order: refer to Reagent Stock Preparations Table for specific volumes.
Add 25 ml of 1 M potassium phosphate buffer (pH 6.0) to the media preparation.
Add 1 ml of 1 M magnesium sulfate to the media preparation.
Add 1 ml of 1 M calcium chloride to the media preparation.
Add 1 ml of cholesterol at a concentration of 5 mg/ml to the media preparation.
Add 250 μL of FUDR at a concentration of 50 mg/ml to the media preparation if required.
Add media manually to each plate or use a calibrated plate-pouring machine.
Allow plates to dry for 24 hours at room temperature or in a hood with the lids on.
Spot the center of each plate with liquid OP50-1 suspension using a pipette.
Stack the spotted plates ‘lid up’ and allow them to dry in a hood with the fan on or on a lab bench for 24 hours.
Transfer dried plates to a tightly-covered plastic standard bin, and store ‘lid up’ in the CITP 20°C incubator for another 24 hours.
Flip plates to store them lid-side down at 4°C.
Mix LB broth Miller granules with agar and water in a 250 mL flask.
Autoclave the mixture and cool it down.
Add streptomycin stock solution to the cooled mixture.
Pipette 50 ml of media into each 10 cm plate.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 16 hours.
Store incubated plates at 4°C.
Streak OP50-1 onto a culture plate.
Remove tube(s) containing the desired strain(s) from -80°C freezer.
Thaw frozen worm tube(s) at room temperature.
Immediately pipette the liquid onto plates.
Pipette 200 µL onto each of two medium plates.
Pipette the remaining 600 µL onto a third medium plate, outside of the bacterial lawn.
Allow plates with lids off to dry in a hood.
Store plates in the 20°C incubator overnight.
Check the plates the next day for viable worms.
Transfer ~50-100 worms to two fresh medium plates.
Transfer 50 eggs to a fresh medium plate (60 mm) twice weekly to maintain strains.
Maintain worms up to two months from their thaw dates in covered plastic boxes at 20°C and 80% humidity.
Create the experiment record in the CITP Data Coordination Center database using the Alpha Time Experiment template.
Set up a one-hour egg lay for each strain with approximately 50 Day 1 or Day 2 gravid adults.
Keep the worms at 20°C during the egg lay.
Record the start time of the egg lay for each plate.
Determine the approximate end time of the egg lay for each plate.
Use the midpoint of the egg lay interval as TELM for α-time calculation.
Transfer one egg per plate onto labeled 3 cm plates on the bacterial lawn after the egg lay.
Obtain at least 20 successful alpha-time observations from 30 starting plates.
Store plates in a covered box in the 20°C incubator until they are ready to check for alpha eggs.
Check every plate once an hour near the expected alpha time for the strain.
Record the time of first observed egg lay (TFE) for each plate.
Keep a data logger with the plates throughout worm development and scoring.
Censor plates if more than five eggs have been laid at the first time of observation (TFE).
Repeat the experiment to observe plates sooner after the initial egg lay if there are more than three out of thirty plates with more than five eggs laid at TFE.
Transfer the adult worm to a fresh plate after 24 hours.
Store the plates from which you transferred the egg-laying worms for two days or until embryos reach L4.
Count the number of progeny worms per plate and record that number on the data sheet or database form.
Repeat steps 4 and 5 until the egg-laying cohort is no longer laying eggs.
Record a final fertility number per subject worm by summing the number of viable progeny for all the days.
Unmate adults one day prior to the egg lay if necessary.
Transfer L4 hermaphrodites from the source plate to a new seeded medium (60 mm) plate if more than 5 males are present.
Flame off males very carefully from the source plate if fewer than 5 males are present.
Use remaining worms only if visual inspection reveals no adult males or signs of mating.
Transfer 50 gravid young adults (day one or two of adulthood) per medium plate.
Remove any eggs or larvae accidentally transferred.
Allow worms to lay eggs for desired time at 20°C, usually around two hours.
Count the eggs laid to ensure there are more than enough for the upcoming assay.
Transfer 40 day-one adults to small (35 mm) FUdR+ plates in triplicate (i.e., 120 animals per strain, minimum).
Keep plates at 20°C with a temperature and humidity data logger when not transferring or scoring.
Transfer living worms to fresh small FUdR+ seeded plates warmed to room temperature.
Score worms according to standard CITP methods.
Transfer worms on days 1(M), 2(TU), and 5(F) of adulthood in Week 1.
Transfer worms on day 8(M), 10(W), and 12(F) of adulthood in Week 2.
Transfer worms on day 15(M) of adulthood in Week 3.
Transfer worms once per week (M) thereafter until all worms are dead.
Score every transfer day and every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
Transfer worms on days 1(TH) and 2(F) of adulthood in Week 1 under the Monday egg lay schedule.
Transfer worms on days 5(M), 7(W), and 9(F) of adulthood in Week 2.
Transfer worms on days 12(M) and 14(W) of adulthood in Week 3.
Transfer worms once per week (W) thereafter until all worms are dead.
Score every transfer day and every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
Continue scoring until all worms are scored as dead or censored.
Run the validation script in the database and resolve any errors.
Attach the temperature and humidity spreadsheet from the data logger to the experiment record in the Filemaker database.
If bacterial contamination is observed, score all worms as lost and mark the “Censor” box for the plate in the database.
Follow the “50% rule” for plates with burrowed worms.
If 50% or more of the worms on a plate have burrowed, then censor that plate on the day the burrowing is observed.
If fewer than 50% of the worms have burrowed, move all the worms on the surface to a fresh plate.
Do not dig into the agar to extract any worms.
Set the plate aside for up to an hour and check it every few minutes to see if any worms have emerged to the surface.
Move any accessible worms to the fresh plate.
Prepare the stock solution.
Sterilize with a 0.22 µm filter and aliquot into sterile tubes.
Thaw stock solution at room temperature.
Mix a working solution by adding 7.5 µL of stock solution to 125 µL of sterile, deionized water per plate.
Spread 132.5 µL of working solution evenly over each plate and allow to dry.
Label the box with the compound set and date.
Store the plates lid-side down at 4°C for no longer than three weeks.
Bring plates to room temperature before transferring worms to them.
Prepare a 192 mM stock solution by adding 0.70 g of powdered compound to 25 mL DI H2O.
Invert the mixing tube to dissolve the compound completely.
Sterilize the solution with 0.22 μm filters into a sterile tube.
Aliquot the stock solution into sterile tubes.
Freeze the tubes for storage at -20°C unless used immediately.
Bring 35 mm FUdR plates to room temperature before use.
Pipette 125 μL of stock solution to each plate.
Gently swirl plates to spread the compound evenly.
Label the box with the compound set and date.
Store the plates lid-side down at 4°C for no longer than three weeks.
Bring plates to room temperature before transferring worms to them.
To prepare a 40 mM aspirin stock solution in DMSO:
Add 36.03 mg of aspirin powder to 5 mL DMSO.
Filter sterilize the solution with 0.22 μm filters into a sterile tube.
Store the filtered solution at -20°C.
Label the box with the compound set and date for aspirin stock solution storage.
Prepare the stock solution of curcumin by adding 73.68 mg powder to 5 mL DMSO.
Sterilize the stock solution using a 0.22 µm PVDF filter and aliquot into sterile tubes.
Thaw the stock solution at room temperature before use.
Bring 35 mm FUdR plates to room temperature prior to adding the compound solution.
Mix a working solution by adding 7.5 μL of stock solution to 125 μL of sterile, deionized water per plate.
Spread 132.5 μL of working solution evenly over each plate and allow to dry.
Label the box with the compound set and date.
Store the plates lid-side down at 4°C for no longer than three weeks.
Prepare a 20 mM stock solution of the compound in DMSO at room temperature by adding 33.6 mg powder to 5 mL DMSO.
Filter sterilize the stock solution using a 0.22 µm PVDF filter.
Aliquot the filtered stock solution into tubes.
Prepare individual aliquots of 7.5 μL of stock solution in small ‘PCR’ tubes.
Add 125 μL of sterile, deionized water to each tube.
Pipette the entirety of this mixture onto the assay plate and distribute evenly across the plate.
Allow the contents on the plate to dry completely.
Label the box with the compound set and date.
Store the plates lid-side down at 4°C for no longer than three weeks.
Bring the plates to room temperature before transferring worms to them.
Thaw the stock solution at room temperature completely.
Prepare individual aliquots of 7.5 μL of stock solution in small ‘PCR’ tubes.
Add 125 μL of sterile, deionized water to each aliquot.
Pipette the entirety of this mixture onto the assay plate and distribute evenly across the plate.
Allow the mixture to dry on the assay plate.
Label the box with the compound set and date.
Store the plates lid-side down at 4°C for no longer than three weeks.
Bring plates to room temperature before transferring worms to them.
Prepare 5 mL of stock solution in DMSO at room temperature by adding 84.88 mg powder to 5 mL DMSO.
Filter sterilize the stock solution with a 0.22 μm filter.
Alquot the filtered stock solution into sterile tubes.
Store the aliquots at -20°C.
Prepare a stock solution of quercetin in DMSO by adding 60.45 mg powder to 5 mL DMSO.
Filter sterilize the stock solution using a 0.22 µm PVDF filter.
Aliquot the filtered stock solution into tubes and store at -20°C.
Bring 35 mm FUdR plates to room temperature before adding compound solution.
Thaw quercetin stock solution completely at room temperature.
Mix 7.5 µL of stock solution with 125 µL of sterile, deionized water per plate to prepare a working solution.
Spread 132.5 μL of the working solution evenly over each FUdR plate and allow it to dry.
Label the box containing the plates with compound set and date.
Store the plates lid-side down at 4°C for no longer than three weeks.
Prepare 45.65 mg of resveratrol powder in 5 mL DMSO at room temperature.
Filter sterilize the prepared stock solution using a 0.22 μm filter.
Aliquot the filtered stock solution into sterile tubes.
Store aliquoted resveratrol stock solution at -20°C.
Bring 35 mm FUdR plates to room temperature prior to adding the compound solution.
Thaw stock solution at room temperature.
Mix a working solution by adding 7.5 μL of stock solution to 125 µL of sterile, deionized water per plate.
Spread 132.5 µL of working solution evenly over each plate and allow to dry.
Label the box with the compound set and date.
Store the plates lid-side down at 4°C for no longer than three weeks.
Add 19.1 mg powdered thioflavin T to 50 mL water to prepare a stock concentration of 1.2 mM.
Filter-sterilize the solution with a 0.22 µm filter and aliquot into sterile 1.5 mL tubes.
Store the aliquoted stock at -20°C unless using immediately.
Bring 35 mm FUdR plates to room temperature.
Pipette 125 μl of stock solution to each plate.
Gently swirl plates to spread compound evenly.
Label the box with the compound set and date.
Store the plates lid-side down at 4°C for no longer than three weeks.
Bring plates to room temperature before transferring worms to them.
Label the box with the compound set and date.
Store the plates lid-side down at 4°C for no longer than three weeks.
Bring plates to room temperature before transferring worms to them.
